correlate.rTableFootnote: Critical value of r (r table), α = .05 {{p3}}: {{p0}} for N = {{p1}} (df = {{p2}}). A correlation larger than this in absolute value is significant.
correlate.rTableFootnoteRange: Critical value of r (r table), α = .05 {{p4}}: {{p0}} for N = {{p1}} up to {{p2}} for N = {{p3}}; each pair is judged by its own N.

regression.ppTitle: Normal P-P Plot of Regression Standardized Residual

assume.title: Classical Assumption Tests
assume.footnote: Computed from the final model's unstandardized residuals, α = .05. Normality, Glejser, Breusch-Pagan and Breusch-Godfrey: Sig. > .05 means the assumption holds. Multicollinearity: VIF < 10 (Tolerance > 0.10). Durbin-Watson: values near 2 suggest no first-order autocorrelation; its test is Breusch-Godfrey. Kolmogorov-Smirnov uses the Lilliefors significance correction.

logistic.notConverged: The model did not converge within the maximum number of iterations — results may be unreliable.
logistic.separation: Perfect or near-perfect separation: some fitted probabilities are numerically 0 or 1, so coefficients and standard errors are unreliable (very large B and SE).
logistic.iterationUnavailable: The iteration history could not be recovered from the model fit.
logistic.hlContingencyTitle: Contingency Table for the Hosmer and Lemeshow Test
logistic.hlUnavailable: The Hosmer-Lemeshow test could not be computed: too few distinct predicted probabilities to form deciles.
logistic.casewiseOutlierFootnote: Cases with a standardized residual (ZResid) greater than {{name}} standard deviations are listed.
logistic.noOutliers: No outliers were found beyond the requested threshold — the casewise list is empty.

curve.title: Model Summary and Parameter Estimates — {{name}}
curve.tooFewCases: {{name}}: fewer than 3 complete cases — no curve could be fit.
curve.modelSkipped: {{p0}} was skipped for {{p1}}: the data does not meet that model's domain requirements (e.g. all values positive, or none equal to zero).

npar.effectSizeFootnote: Positive values mean group {{p0}} ranks higher than group {{p1}}. r = |Z|/√N (Rosenthal); rank-biserial r is the net proportion of non-overlapping pairs (-1 to +1). Hodges-Lehmann is the median of all pairwise differences ({{p0}} - {{p1}}), in the variable’s own units.
npar.pairwiseFootnote: Each row tests the null hypothesis that the distributions of Sample 1 and Sample 2 are the same. Asymptotic significances (2-sided tests) are displayed. The significance level is .05; Adj. Sig. values are Bonferroni-corrected for multiple tests.

nparBinomial.title: Binomial Test
nparBinomial.noteWeightRounded: Weighted counts were rounded to the nearest integer for the exact binomial test.

nparKS.title: One-Sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov Test
nparKS.lillieforsWarning: Mean and SD were estimated from this sample. The classical Kolmogorov-Smirnov p-value is liberal (too small) in this case — install the 'nortest' R package (setup.R) for a Lilliefors-corrected p-value, available in the Normality tab.

roc.dirLargerNote: Larger values of the test result variable(s) indicate stronger evidence for a positive actual state.
roc.dirSmallerNote: Smaller values of the test result variable(s) indicate stronger evidence for a positive actual state.
roc.seMethodNoteNegexp: The standard error of the area was computed under the bi-negative exponential assumption (Hanley & McNeil 1982); the {{name}}% interval is area ± z × SE. That assumption holds only if the test scores are exponentially distributed — the Nonparametric option makes no such assumption. The significance test uses the standard error under H₀ (area = 0.5).
roc.tiesNote: The test result variable(s) {{name}} have at least one tie between the positive actual state group and the negative actual state group. Statistics may be biased.
roc.aucFootnote: a. Under the nonparametric assumption. b. Null hypothesis: true area = 0.5.
roc.aucFootnoteNegexp: a. Under the bi-negative exponential assumption. b. Null hypothesis: true area = 0.5.
roc.cutoffFootnote: The smallest cutoff value is the minimum observed test value minus 1, and the largest cutoff value is the maximum observed test value plus 1. All the other cutoff values are the averages of two consecutive ordered observed test values.
roc.youdenFootnote: Youden's J = Sensitivity + Specificity − 1; the cut-off with the largest J. PPV and NPV depend on the proportion of positives in this sample and do not carry over directly to a population with a different prevalence. LR+ = Sensitivity / (1 − Specificity), LR− = (1 − Sensitivity) / Specificity; left blank where the denominator is zero.
roc.youdenTiesNote: {{name}}: more than one cut-off reaches the same maximum Youden's J; all are listed. The plot marks the smallest.
roc.youdenCiTitle: Bootstrap Confidence Intervals for the Optimal Cut-off
roc.youdenCiFootnote: Percentile bootstrap, {{name}} stratified resamples (positive and negative group sizes kept), fixed seed. The optimal point is re-selected in every resample; the cut-off's interval is usually wide — it shows how unstable the threshold is.
roc.youdenCiNoWeight: Youden bootstrap confidence interval skipped: case weighting is on and the bootstrap does not support weighted cases. The optimal cut-off table uses the weights.
roc.youdenCiNoPackage: Youden bootstrap confidence interval skipped: the 'pROC' R package was not found.

rocAnalysis.imbalanceNote: {{name}}: the positive class is under 10% of cases — consider the Precision-Recall curve alongside the ROC curve.
rocAnalysis.compareFootnote: DeLong, DeLong & Clarke-Pearson (1988) nonparametric test for paired ROC curves — every test variable compared against the same cases/state variable.
rocAnalysis.compareAucNoWeight: AUC comparison (DeLong) was requested but skipped — the 'pROC' package's DeLong test has no weighted-case support, and a case weight is currently active. Turn off weighting to use this option.
rocAnalysis.compareAucNoPackage: AUC comparison (DeLong) was requested, but the 'pROC' R package is not installed — install it from Utilities → R Packages to use this option.
rocAnalysis.seMethodNote: The standard error of the area was computed under the nonparametric assumption (the Hanley & McNeil variance with Q1 and Q2 estimated from the data — the method SPSS uses); the {{name}}% interval is area ± z × SE. The significance test uses a different standard error: the one under H₀ (area = 0.5). They are not the same value, so the interval and the p-value are read independently.
rocAnalysis.prAucFootnote: Area under the interpolated Precision-Recall curve (trapezoids over recall). Read it against the no-skill baseline, which equals the share of positive cases.
rocAnalysis.modelQualityNote: Overall Model Quality shows the lower bound of the {{name}}% confidence interval of each area. A good model has a value above 0.5; a value below 0.5 means the model does no better than random guessing.

survival.medianTitle: Means and Medians for Survival Time
survival.needsPackage: Survival analysis requires the R 'survival' package. Run setup.R.
survival.medianCiNote: The median is the smallest observed time at which the survival estimate reaches 0.5. The 95% limits come from inverting the confidence band for S(t) (Greenwood variance, log transform) at 0.5; the linear median ± 1.96 × SE(median) approximation was not used — the two can separate noticeably in a heavily censored tail.
survival.tableTruncated: The survival table was cut off at the first 5000 rows — the full table is too large for the output view.
survival.pairwiseNoAdjustNote: Pairwise comparisons are not adjusted for multiple testing: each row is a two-sample test in its own right. With k groups there are k(k-1)/2 of them, so the chance of at least one false positive is above the nominal level.
survival.noStrataForMode: No strata variable was assigned, so "for each stratum" could not be applied; the comparison was run over the whole sample.
survival.meanRestrictedNote: The mean is the RESTRICTED mean, limited to each group's own largest observed time. When that time is censored the true mean is larger, which is why an unrestricted mean is not reported.

cox.tiesEfronNote: The data has tied event times ({{name}} repeated time(s)): the partial likelihood was computed with Efron's tie correction. Tie handling is a method choice — Breslow's correction gives slightly different values for −2LL, the LR chi-square and the coefficients.
cox.stepOmnibusTitle: Omnibus Tests of Model Coefficients by Step
cox.phTestTitle: Test of the Proportional Hazards Assumption
cox.phNote: Grambsch-Therneau test: scaled Schoenfeld residuals correlated with time. A small p means that variable's hazard ratio is not constant over follow-up — the assumption the model rests on. Consider stratifying on it, or modelling a time-dependent effect.
cox.contrastNote: {{p0}}: {{p1}} contrast coding, reference category "{{p2}}". What the coefficients mean depends on the coding — a different one gives different B values from the same data.
cox.refModalNote: Curves are drawn with scale covariates held at their means and categorical ones at their most frequent category (the mean of a set of dummies is not a case that can exist).
cox.refMeanNote: Curves are drawn with the covariates held at their means.
cox.stepLRNote: Stepwise selection used the partial likelihood-ratio (LR) statistic for both entry and removal.
cox.stepWaldNote: Stepwise selection used the partial likelihood-ratio (LR) statistic for entry and the Wald statistic for removal.
cox.stepLimit: Stepwise selection reached its step limit; the model is reported as it stood at that point.
cox.coefInfinite: The Cox fit reported a non-converged or infinite coefficient (often complete separation); the estimates and standard errors are unreliable.
cox.noTermsEntered: No covariate met the entry criterion — the model is empty.
cox.baselineUnavailable: The baseline function table could not be computed for this model.
cox.phUnavailable: The proportional hazards test could not be computed for this model.
cox.plotUnavailable: The plots could not be computed for this model.
cox.separateNotCategorical: The variable chosen for separate lines is not a categorical covariate in this model; a single curve was drawn.
cox.epvWarn: The model has only {{p0}} events for {{p1}} coefficients. Below about 10 events per coefficient, the estimates and their confidence intervals can be biased.
cox.schoenfeldNotAligned: Schoenfeld residuals could not be matched to cases, so they were not written as new variables. The other requested variables are unaffected.

reliability.splitFootnote: Part 1: {{p0}} · Part 2: {{p1}}. The scale is split by item order; with an odd number of items the extra item goes to Part 1.
reliability.warnSplitItems: Split-half model not computed: each half needs at least two items for its own alpha, so the scale must have at least four.
reliability.guttmanFootnote: Guttman's (1945) lower bounds of reliability. Lambda 4 splits the items in two by their order (the first half may take one more item).
reliability.fitTitle: Test for Goodness of Fit of Model
reliability.logDetUnconstrained: Log of determinant of unconstrained matrix
reliability.logDetConstrained: Log of determinant of constrained matrix
reliability.fitFootnote: Likelihood-ratio chi-square: n (ln|Σ̂| − ln|S|), with S and Σ̂ the maximum likelihood (divisor n) covariances.
reliability.strictStatsTitle: Statistics under Strictly Parallel Model Assumption
reliability.omegaFootnote: ω (total) from a one-factor model (maximum likelihood): (Σλ)² / ((Σλ)² + Σθ).
reliability.omegaFailed: ω could not be computed: the one-factor model did not converge.
reliability.hotellingN: Hotelling's T² needs more cases than items.
reliability.cochranBinary: Cochran's test needs 0/1 items; the F test is shown instead.
reliability.tukeyPower: Tukey's estimate of power to which observations must be raised to achieve additivity = {{name}}.
reliability.iccFootnote: Model: {{p0}}; type: {{p1}}; F test against a true value of {{p2}} (McGraw & Wong, 1996).
reliability.rTableFootnote: Critical value of r (r table), α = .05 two-tailed: {{p0}} for N = {{p1}} (df = {{p2}}). Items whose Corrected Item-Total Correlation falls below it are usually read as not valid.

glmUni.title: Tests of Between-Subjects Effects — {{name}}
glmUni.type4Note: Type IV Sum of Squares was computed identically to Type III for this design, which has no missing cells.
glmUni.homogTitle: Levene's Test of Equality of Error Variances — {{name}}
glmUni.paramFootnote: This parameter is set to zero by this coding convention (last category taken as reference); B values are coding-dependent.

glmMulti.boxTitle: Box's Test of Equality of Covariance Matrices
glmMulti.boxFootnote: Tests the null hypothesis that the observed covariance matrices of the dependent variables are equal across groups.
glmMulti.boxSkippedNote: Box's M: {{name}} cell(s) with a singular covariance matrix (too few cases) were left out, as SPSS does.
glmMulti.boxNotComputed: Box's M was not computed: fewer than two cells have a non-singular covariance matrix.
glmMulti.royFootnote: Roy's Largest Root F is an upper bound on F that yields a lower bound on the significance level.

glmRep.mvNotComputed: Multivariate tests were not computed: too few error degrees of freedom.
glmRep.mauchlyFootnote: Tests the null hypothesis that the error covariance matrix of the orthonormalized transformed dependent variables is proportional to an identity matrix.
glmRep.leveneTitle: Levene's Test of Equality of Error Variances
glmRep.leveneFootnote: Based on the mean. Tests the null hypothesis that the error variance of each dependent variable is equal across groups.
glmRep.pairwiseFootnote: Based on estimated marginal means. Adjustment for multiple comparisons: {{name}}.
glmRep.adjLsd: Least Significant Difference (equivalent to no adjustment)

factor.bartlettChiLabel: Bartlett's Test of Sphericity — Approx. Chi-Square
factor.matrixFootnote: Extraction Method: Principal Component Analysis. Components with eigenvalue > 1.
factor.rotatedMatrixFootnote: Extraction Method: Principal Component Analysis. Rotation Method: Varimax with Kaiser Normalization.
factor.rotationSSTitle: Total Variance Explained — Rotation Sums of Squared Loadings
factor.obliqueMatrixFootnote: Extraction Method: Principal Component Analysis. Rotation Method: Oblique (factors are correlated — see Factor Correlation Matrix).
factor.scoresSingular: Factor scores could not be computed: the correlation matrix is singular — some variables are perfectly collinear.
factor.antiImageFootnote: Diagonal: each item's Measure of Sampling Adequacy (MSA). Off-diagonal: negative partial correlations.
factor.lowMsaNote: Items with a Measure of Sampling Adequacy below .50: {{name}}. They are candidates for removal from the factor analysis.
factor.antiImageSingular: The anti-image matrix could not be computed: the correlation matrix is singular (some variables are perfectly collinear).
factor.polychoricFallback: Polychoric correlations could not be used (items must be integers with at most 10 categories); Pearson correlations were used.
factor.polychoricNote: The analysis used the polychoric correlation matrix (items treated as categorized versions of a continuous trait). Factor scores are computed from the standardized raw scores.
factor.parallelNone: By parallel analysis no factor's eigenvalue exceeds that of random data; one factor is shown anyway. The data may have no common structure.
factor.tooManyFactors: The requested number of factors cannot be extracted from this many variables; {{name}} factors were extracted.
factor.notConverged: Extraction did not converge in {{name}} iterations; results are from the last iteration. Raise the iteration limit or extract fewer factors.
factor.heywood: Variable(s) with a communality of 1 or more (Heywood case): {{name}}. The solution may be invalid; change the number of factors or the method.
factor.commFootnote: Extraction Method: {{name}}. Initial communalities are squared multiple correlations (SMC).
factor.parallelFootnote: Horn's parallel analysis: the eigenvalues of the correlation matrix were compared with those of {{p0}} random normal data sets of the same size (n, number of variables). Factors whose eigenvalue exceeds the random 95th percentile are retained: {{p1}}.
factor.suppressNote: Loadings with an absolute value below {{name}} are suppressed.
factor.lowLoadingNote: Items with no loading of .30 or more on any factor: {{name}}.
factor.crossLoadingNote: Cross-loading items (loading above .30 on two factors, less than .10 apart): {{name}}.
factor.sigPearsonFootnote: Significance levels are for the Pearson correlations; polychoric correlations have no comparable test.
factor.inverseSingular: The inverse of the correlation matrix could not be computed: the matrix is singular (some variables are perfectly collinear).
factor.residualFootnote: Residuals are computed between observed and reproduced correlations. There are {{p0}} ({{p1}}%) nonredundant residuals with absolute values greater than 0.05.
factor.pairwiseNote: Missing values were excluded pairwise: each correlation uses the cases valid on both variables. The chi-square tests use the smallest pairwise N ({{name}}).
factor.meanSubNote: Missing values were replaced with the variable mean.
factor.scoresPairwiseNote: Factor scores were computed only for cases with no missing value.
factor.covarianceNote: The analysis used the covariance matrix: raw loadings are in the units of the variables, rescaled loadings are correlations with the factors.
factor.covarianceMethod: This extraction method cannot analyze a covariance matrix (only principal components, principal axis factoring and image factoring can); the correlation matrix was used.
factor.covTveFootnote: Percentages of the raw sums are of the total variance (the sum of the variances); the rescaled sums are of the number of variables.
factor.rescSSTotal: Rescaled Extraction Sums of Squared Loadings
factor.rawSSTotal: Raw Rotation Sums of Squared Loadings
factor.kappaInvalid: Kappa must be at least 1; the default 4 was used.
factor.rotNotConverged: The rotation did not converge in {{name}} iterations; results are from the last iteration.
factor.rotationFailed: The rotation could not be computed; only the unrotated solution is shown.
factor.extractionFailed: The extraction failed: too many factors were requested for these variables (no valid communalities exist). Extract fewer factors or use principal components.
factor.imageSingular: Image factoring needs a nonsingular correlation matrix: some variables are perfectly collinear.
factor.scoresHeywood: Bartlett and Anderson-Rubin scores could not be computed: a variable has a uniqueness of zero (Heywood case). Use the regression method or change the solution.
factor.scoreCoefFootnote: Extraction Method: {{p0}}. Score method: {{p1}}. Coefficients apply to the standardized variables (to the centered variables in a covariance analysis).
factor.loadingPlotOne: Only one factor was extracted; a loading plot needs at least two.

kmeans.notConverged: K-means did not converge within 50 iterations; the clusters are provisional.
kmeans.sizesTitle: Number of Cases in each Cluster

discriminant.needsPackage: Discriminant analysis requires the R 'MASS' package. Run setup.R.

knn.classFootnote: Leave-one-out cross-validated classification (each case predicted using all others, not itself) — an honest accuracy estimate, unlike resubstitution.
knn.needsPackage: Nearest Neighbor requires the R 'class' package. Run setup.R.

tree.riskFootnote: Resubstitution risk estimate (1 − accuracy on the training data) with its standard error — the growing method is CRT (rpart); SPSS's CHAID/QUEST are not implemented (no equivalent base/recommended R package).
tree.classFootnote: Resubstitution classification (each case predicted by the fitted tree, matching SPSS Tree's own default; the tree's minCases/maxDepth stopping rules bound overfitting, unlike a pure-memorization method).
tree.needsPackage: Decision Tree requires the R 'rpart' package. Run setup.R.

multinom.refFootnote: The reference category is the first category.
multinom.needsPackage: Multinomial regression requires the R 'nnet' package. Run setup.R.

extra.notConverged: The model did not converge. Interpret estimates and tests with caution; increase iterations or revise the model.
extra.halvingFailed: Step-halving could not improve the likelihood.
extra.separation: Possible separation detected: extreme coefficients and near-zero fitted probabilities. This is a numerical diagnostic, not a proof of separation.
extra.aliased: Redundant design columns were excluded using the singularity tolerance.
extra.unreliableEstimates: The standard error (and the resulting Wald/Sig/CI values) could not be reliably estimated for some coefficients because of near-complete separation; those cells are shown as missing.
extra.deltaApplied: Delta was added to zero response cells for estimation.
extra.sparseCells: Some expected cell counts are below 5; asymptotic goodness-of-fit tests may be unreliable.
extra.weightedCounts: Category counts are weighted; valid and excluded case counts are unweighted.
extra.associationFootnote: Each non-reference category is compared with the reference using its fitted conditional probability.
extra.parameterLimit: Model exceeds 1500 estimable parameters; reduce the interaction terms.
extra.factorLimit: Full factorial models support at most eight factors.
extra.missingTerm: A custom model term uses an unavailable predictor.

crosstabs.warnFisherMonteCarlo: Fisher's exact test could not be computed exactly for this table; the value shown is a Monte Carlo estimate (fixed seed, 20,000 replicates).
crosstabs.measuresFootnote: Significance for ordinal measures uses the tie-corrected normal approximation under independence (a test that the measure equals 0).
crosstabs.warnNominal2x2: Nominal measures require at least a 2×2 table.
crosstabs.warnOrdinal2x2: Ordinal measures require at least a 2×2 table.
crosstabs.warnOrdinalOrder: Ordinal measures assume category order; non-numeric categories were ordered alphabetically.
crosstabs.chiSqFootnote: {{p0}} cells ({{p1}}%) have expected count less than 5. The minimum expected count is {{p2}}.
crosstabs.warnExactWeighted: Fisher's exact test is not computed when case weights are active (exact tests require integer counts).
crosstabs.warnMcnemarCategories: McNemar test not computed: both variables must have identical category values (McNemar compares two measurements of the same trait).
crosstabs.warnKappaCategories: Kappa not computed: the row and column variables must have identical category values (Kappa measures agreement between two ratings of the same categories). Pairing the categories by position would produce a number here, but it would not be an agreement measure.
crosstabs.colPropFootnote: Categories of {{name}} sharing a letter have column proportions that do not differ significantly from each other at the .05 level (two-proportion z-test). ".": this category is not used in comparisons because its column proportion is equal to zero or one.
crosstabs.colPropFootnoteBonf: Categories of {{name}} sharing a letter have column proportions that do not differ significantly from each other at the .05 level (two-proportion z-test, Bonferroni-adjusted). ".": this category is not used in comparisons because its column proportion is equal to zero or one.
crosstabs.colPropPairsFootnote: Within each row category, the column proportions of {{name}} are compared pairwise: z = (p₁ − p₂) / √(p(1 − p)(1/n₁ + 1/n₂)), p the pooled proportion. The Bonferroni adjustment multiplies p by the number of comparisons in that row (at most 1).

explore.noteWeightPartial: Case weights were applied to the Descriptives table only; other Explore output is unweighted.
explore.mEstimatorsFootnote: Weighting constants: Huber 1.339 · Tukey 4.685 · Hampel 1.700 / 3.400 / 8.500 · Andrews 1.340*pi. M-Estimators cannot be computed for distributions with zero spread around the median (MAD = 0). The location estimate is an iteratively reweighted least-squares (IRLS) fit; the scale is the median absolute deviation from the median, held fixed across all iterations (not the normal-consistency-corrected MAD).
explore.warnNortestMissing: The 'nortest' R package is not installed; Kolmogorov-Smirnov used the uncorrected (asymptotic) p-value. Run setup.R to enable the Lilliefors correction.
explore.warnMassMissing: M-Estimators were requested, but the MASS R package is not installed — this table was skipped.

freq.warnNonNumericStats: Some values of “{{name}}” could not be converted to numbers (a non-numeric/categorical variable); numeric statistics such as mean, sum and std. deviation were not computed for it.

mixed.type1Title: Type I Tests of Fixed Effects
mixed.sumCodingFootnote: Factors use sum-to-zero (effect) coding: each coefficient is a level's deviation from the average over levels; the last level is not shown.
mixed.covCiNotComputed: Confidence intervals for the covariance parameters could not be computed (the variance estimate is at its boundary).
mixed.dfNote: Denominator degrees of freedom follow nlme's containment rule, not SPSS's Satterthwaite approximation; estimates, standard errors and t values are unaffected, and p-values can differ slightly from SPSS's.

lifetab.seCumSurv: Std. Error of Cumulative Proportion Surviving at End of Interval

missing.mcarUnavailable: Little's MCAR test could not be computed for this data.
missing.mcarFootnote: Little's MCAR test: Chi-Square = {{p0}}, df = {{p1}}, Sig. = {{p2}}
missing.listwiseEmpty: Listwise estimates were not computed: fewer than two complete cases.
missing.emFailed: EM estimates could not be computed.
missing.regressionNotComputed: Regression estimates were not computed: too few complete cases.
missing.tTestFootnote: Indicator variables with less than {{name}}% missing are not displayed.
missing.mismatchFootnote: The diagonal is the percentage of missing values of each variable; off-diagonal cells are the percentage of cases where one variable is missing and the other is not.

gee.needsPackage: GEE requires the R 'geepack' package. Run setup.R.

glmm.needsPackage: GLMM requires the R 'lme4' package. Install it from Utilities → R Packages.

mi.needsPackage: Multiple Imputation requires the R 'mice' package. Install it from Utilities → R Packages.
mi.pooledFootnote: The pooled estimate combines the imputations by Rubin's (1987) rules; the interval uses the t distribution with df = (m−1)(1 + ū/((1+1/m)B))². The degrees of freedom fall — and the interval widens — as the fraction of missing information rises.

bayes.needsPackage: Bayesian analysis requires the R 'BayesFactor' package. Install it from Utilities → R Packages.
bayes.priorFootnote: The Bayes factor was computed with a Cauchy prior of width r = {{p1}} on the effect size ({{p0}}). The width moves the result directly: on the same data a wider prior penalises the alternative more and lowers BF₁₀. It can be changed in the analysis dialog.
bayes.mcmcNote: The posterior summary is estimated from {{p0}} Monte Carlo (MCMC) draws with random seed {{p1}}, so running the analysis again on the same data gives the same values. The Bayes factor itself does not depend on the draws.

reportSummaries.title: Report
reportSummaries.limitNote: Listing limited to the first {{p0}} of {{p1}} cases; the summary lines cover every case.

newVars.created: {{name}} added to the dataset as new variables. The file was not saved — Ctrl+Z undoes this.
newVars.failed: Could not create the new variables; the dataset is unchanged: {{name}}
newVars.noDataset: Could not create new variables: no dataset is open.
newVars.datasetChanged: Could not create the new variables: the analysis ran on a dataset that is no longer the active one.

cfa.title: Confirmatory Factor Analysis
cfa.identMarker: The first indicator's loading on each factor is fixed at 1.
cfa.estimatorAuto: Estimator chosen automatically: {{name}} (WLSMV when the items are ordinal or have at most 5 categories, else ML).
cfa.someContinuous: Items with more than 10 categories are modelled as continuous under WLSMV.
cfa.wlsmvPairwise: WLSMV has no FIML; missing values were handled pairwise.
cfa.crossLoadingNote: Some items load on more than one factor (cross-loadings).
cfa.notConverged: The model did not converge; parameter estimates are not trustworthy and are not shown. Simplify the model or use a larger sample.
cfa.fitFootnote: Cut-offs: Hu & Bentler (1999); Schermelleh-Engel, Moosbrugger & Müller (2003). They are rules of thumb; judge several indices together.
cfa.fitFootnoteRobust: Robust column: scaled χ² and robust CFI/TLI/RMSEA; the assessment uses this column. Cut-offs: Hu & Bentler (1999); Schermelleh-Engel et al. (2003).
cfa.loadingsFootnoteMarker: Indicators whose loading is fixed at 1 have no standard error or p value.
cfa.lowLoadings: Items with a standardized loading below .50: {{name}}.
cfa.deltaFootnote: Residual variances of ordinal items are not estimated; they follow as 1 − R².
cfa.heywood: Heywood case (negative residual variance or standardized loading above 1): {{name}}. The solution is improper; revise the model.
cfa.reliabilityFootnote: CR: composite reliability (≥ .70); AVE: average variance extracted (≥ .50); MSV: maximum shared variance (should be below AVE). From the standardized solution (Fornell & Larcker, 1981; Hair et al.).
cfa.fornellFootnote: Diagonal: √AVE; off-diagonal: factor correlations. For discriminant validity each √AVE should exceed the correlations in its row and column.
cfa.htmtFootnote: Heterotrait-monotrait ratio (Henseler, Ringle & Sarstedt, 2015). For discriminant validity below .85 (strict) or .90.
cfa.htmtHigh: Factor pairs with HTMT of .85 or above: {{name}}.
cfa.miFootnote: Largest indices with MI ≥ {{name}}. → is a new loading, ↔ an error covariance. Add a parameter only with a theoretical reason.
cfa.invFailed: An invariance model could not be fitted: {{name}}
cfa.invFootnote: Each model is compared with the previous one. Decision: ΔCFI ≥ −.010 (Cheung & Rensvold, 2002) and ΔRMSEA ≤ .015 (Chen, 2007). Δχ² flags even small differences in large samples.
cfa.invFootnoteOrdinal: Ordinal items: the scalar step equates thresholds and there is no strict step. Δχ² is the scaled difference test. Decision: ΔCFI ≥ −.010 and ΔRMSEA ≤ .015.

itemAnalysis.title: Item Analysis
itemAnalysis.alphaFootnote: Cronbach's alpha (all items) = {{name}}. Floor / ceiling: percentage of answers at the lowest / highest value the items take.
itemAnalysis.lowItemTotal: Items with a corrected item-total correlation below .30: {{name}}.
itemAnalysis.alphaRises: Items whose removal would raise alpha: {{name}}.
itemAnalysis.tiesAtCut: Cases with tied totals straddle a group boundary; which of the tied cases joined the group follows the data order.
itemAnalysis.ulFootnote: {{p0}} cases per group; lower group totals {{p1}}–{{p2}}, upper group {{p3}}–{{p4}}. Independent-samples t test (Welch).
itemAnalysis.ulNotSig: Items that do not separate the upper and lower groups (p ≥ .05): {{name}}.
itemAnalysis.difficultyFootnote: p: proportion correct; D = p(upper) − p(lower). Ebel (1965): D ≥ .40 very good; .30–.39 good; .20–.29 needs revision; < .20 poor.
itemAnalysis.listwise: {{name}} cases with a missing answer were excluded.

likert.title: Likert Item Descriptives
likert.pctFootnote: Row percentages; each item over its own answered cases.
likert.reverseFootnote: (R): reverse-scored item. Frequencies are the answers given; mean, SD and level use the reversed scores.
likert.intervalFootnote: Interval width = ({{p0}} − {{p1}}) / {{p2}} = {{p3}}. A mean on a boundary falls in the lower interval.
likert.offScale: {{name}} values lie outside the response range and were not counted.

scale.title: Scale Scores Report
scale.corrTitle: Means, Standard Deviations, Reliabilities and Correlations
scale.corrFootnote: Diagonal: Cronbach's alpha; below it: Pearson r; above it: two-tailed p.
scale.scoreMean: Score: mean of the items, for cases that answered all of them.
scale.scoreMeanR: Score: mean of the items, for cases that answered all of them. (R) items reversed as {{name}} − score.
scale.scoreSum: Score: sum of the items, for cases that answered all of them.
scale.scoreSumR: Score: sum of the items, for cases that answered all of them. (R) items reversed as {{name}} − score.

harman.title: Harman's Single-Factor Test
harman.varTitle: Variance Explained by a Single Factor
harman.footnote: {{p0}} items, {{p1}} complete cases. Harman's test is a weak diagnostic: below 50% does not prove the absence of common method variance (Podsakoff et al., 2003).
harman.cfaFootnote: All items on one factor (maximum likelihood). Poor fit indicates that a single method factor does not account for the data.

retest.title: Test-Retest Reliability
retest.footnote: ICC: single measures, {{p0}}, {{p1}} (Koo & Li, 2016: < .50 poor; .50–.75 moderate; .75–.90 good; > .90 excellent). t, df, p: paired-samples t test.
retest.tooFew: {{name}} needs at least three complete cases; the pair was skipped.

lawshe.footExact: CVR = (ne − N/2) / (N/2); code for essential: {{name}}. Critical value: exact binomial, one-tailed α = .05 (Ayre & Scally, 2014). An item is retained when CVR ≥ the critical value.
lawshe.footLawshe: CVR = (ne − N/2) / (N/2); code for essential: {{name}}. Critical value: Lawshe's (1975) table; an N between its rows takes the next smaller (stricter) row. An item is retained when CVR ≥ the critical value.
lawshe.cviFootnote: CVI: mean CVR of the retained items. A CVI at or above the critical CVR is taken as adequate content validity for the scale.
lawshe.fewExperts: Some items were rated by fewer than five experts; the CVR is not dependable at that size.
lawshe.noEssential: No cell holds the code for essential; check the code you entered.

doe.title: Design of Experiments Analysis
doe.cvSplit: CV(a) = {{p0}}%, CV(b) = {{p1}}%; grand mean = {{p2}}. Block and the main-plot factor are tested against error (a), the others against error (b).
doe.excluded: {{name}} plots with a missing value were excluded.
doe.unbalanced: The design is unbalanced (missing or extra observations); sums of squares are sequential (Type I) and depend on the term order.
doe.meansFootnote: {{p0}}, α = {{p1}}; error MS = {{p2}}, df = {{p3}} ({{p5}}); critical difference = {{p4}}. Means sharing a letter do not differ.
doe.splitCompareNote: The main-plot factor is compared with error (a), the sub-plot factor and the combinations with error (b). The combination comparisons hold between sub-plot levels; comparing main-plot levels at the same sub-plot level needs a pooled error.
doe.effectsFootnote: Effect = 2 × coefficient (−1 / +1 coding). t tests on {{name}} error degrees of freedom.
doe.lenthFootnote: Unreplicated design: no error degrees of freedom. Lenth (1989): PSE = {{p0}}, ME = {{p1}}, SME = {{p2}} (α = .05).
doe.paretoCritT: Dashed line on the Pareto chart: the two-tailed critical t value.
doe.paretoCritMe: Dashed line on the Pareto chart: Lenth's ME.

computeInfo.title: Compute Variable
computeInfo.body: SAI computes variables with spreadsheet formulas in the Data View. Add (or pick) a column, type a formula like =weight/(height*height) in its first cell, then fill it down. The computed values are saved to the dataset. (An SPSS-style COMPUTE command line is planned.)

r.intro: A persistent R session with your dataset pre-loaded as a read-only `data` frame. Same R engine as the menus — identical code, identical output.
r.staleHint: The dataset has changed since this session started. The R console's `data` still reflects the old state — click to refresh it.

r.sees1: `data` — a copy of the current dataset (read-only).
r.sees2: The shared R library — packages you install stay available.
r.sees3: Its own working directory — you can write to your own files freely.
r.caution1: Edits in the grid / menus / SPSS syntax don't auto-refresh `data` — call sai_data().
r.caution2: Changes in R are not written to the open dataset; use sai_commit(df) to open a data frame as a new dataset.
r.caution3: Session state is hidden — restart R and re-run top-to-bottom for reproducibility.
r.caution4: A long or infinite loop can lock the session — recover with Restart.

doe.createHint_latin: t × t square: each treatment once in every row and column (3–12 treatments).
doe.createHint_factorial: All combinations of the factor levels, completely randomized or in blocks.
doe.createHint_splitplot: Main-plot factor randomized within blocks; sub-plot factor randomized within each main plot.
doe.createHint_twok: k factors at two levels (−1 / +1); run order randomized, standard order kept in its own column.
doe.blockedOption: Lay the combinations out in blocks (one replicate per block)
doe.sizePreview: The design has {{n}} plots (rows) and opens as a new dataset; fill in the response column after the experiment.
doe.errFactorNames: Every factor needs its own name.
doe.errResponseName: Give the response column a name different from the factors.
doe.errSeed: The seed must be a whole number.
doe.errTwoLevels: In a 2^k design every factor needs two levels (low, high).
doe.errLevels: Every factor needs at least two distinct levels.
doe.errReplicates: Replicates / blocks must be a whole number from 2 to 100 (1 is allowed for 2^k and factorial designs).
